subject: chemistry_2
question_text: Give the source of the following vitamins and name the disease caused by their deficiency.

verification.note: Unit 13 (Biomolecules) is sourced from the chemistry half of "FAST TRACK IPE for Sr. Students", printed chapter 10 "BIOMOLECULES", book pp.99-104; the book prints this question on book p.103 as SAQ 10. The 1+1+1+1 mark split is a CLAIM, not the board's, until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. Neither the two-book union check nor a board back-test was possible for Chemistry-II: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is physics-only and first-year, and no second-year chemistry paper is in the corpus. BOOK TYPO, corrected here: the printed table gives the vitamin E deficiency as "Sterility, Neurosis of heart muscles". The word is necrosis, the death of tissue; neurosis is unrelated. NEEDS TEACHER RULING (vitamin E deficiency): the guide's "sterility, necrosis of heart muscles" and NCERT Class 12 Table 14.5's "increased fragility of RBCs and muscular weakness" are different answers to the same cell. Both are printed on the card, NCERT's first, until a Telangana IPE teacher says which the key marks; neither is asserted here as the sole answer. The book prints this as a three-column table (Vitamin / Source / Deficiency disease); it is written here as ordinary lines because the notebook page is ruled, and a student may still lay it out as a table in the examination. The printed question ends with a question mark after a command sentence; that is dropped in question_text.

steps.label: Vitamin A
lines: Sources: fish liver oil, carrots, butter and
Deficiency: xerophthalmia, which is a drying
of the eye, and night blindness.
steps.why: Vitamin A is used to make the pigment of the retina that responds to dim light, so the earliest sign of a shortage is difficulty seeing at night. Carrots are the plant source because they contain carotene, which the body converts into vitamin A.
common_mistakes: Naming scurvy or rickets for vitamin A. Those belong to vitamins C and D.
Writing only the disease. The question asks for the source as well, so both are needed for each mark.
steps.memory_tip: A is for the eye: night blindness when it is short.
steps.margin_note: Two items per vitamin: source and disease. Lay it out as a table if there is room on the page.

steps.label: Vitamin D
lines: Sources: fish, egg yolk, and the action of
steps.why: Vitamin D controls the uptake of calcium, so a shortage gives soft, weak bone. The same shortage is named differently by age: rickets while the bones are still growing, osteomalacia after they have stopped, and both names are expected.
common_mistakes: Giving rickets for adults. In adults the disease is osteomalacia; rickets is the disease of children.
Leaving out sunlight as a source. Vitamin D is made in the skin in sunlight, and that is part of the answer.
steps.memory_tip: D is for bone: rickets in the child, osteomalacia in the adult.
steps.margin_note: Both names are wanted here, one for each age group. They are the marked part of this step.

steps.label: Vitamin E
lines: Sources: vegetable oils such as sunflower
oil, green leafy vegetables, egg yolk.
Deficiency: increased fragility of the red
Some texts give it as sterility and
steps.why: Vitamin E is fat soluble and is found with the fats and oils of the diet, which is why vegetable oils head its source list. It protects the membrane of the red blood cell, so a shortage makes those cells fragile and weakens the muscles. Some texts give the deficiency instead as sterility and necrosis, meaning the death of tissue, in the heart muscle, so both wordings are worth knowing.
common_mistakes: Writing neurosis for necrosis, if you use that wording. Necrosis means the death of tissue; neurosis is a different word altogether.
Naming a bone or eye disease for vitamin E. Its deficiency shows in the red blood cells and in the muscles; the eye and the bone belong to vitamins A and D.
steps.memory_tip: E is found in the oils; short of it the red blood cells become fragile and the muscles weaken.
steps.margin_note: Give the source and the deficiency. Spell necrosis carefully if you use that word; it is a different word from neurosis.

steps.label: Vitamin K

lines.text: A, D, E and K are the fat soluble vitamins

lines: Sources: green leafy vegetables, cow milk,
steps.why: Vitamin K is needed to make several of the proteins that carry out clotting, so a shortage shows as blood that takes longer than normal to clot rather than as a named disease. All four vitamins on this list are the fat soluble group, which is why they are asked together.
common_mistakes: Naming a disease for vitamin K. The deficiency effect is a longer clotting time, not a named disease.
Writing that vitamin K is water soluble. A, D, E and K are the fat soluble vitamins.
steps.memory_tip: K is the clotting vitamin; short of it, the blood is slow to clot.
steps.margin_note: Eight items in all, two for each of four vitamins. Count them before you move on.

insider_note: Four vitamins, two items each, eight items in all. A table is the fastest layout and makes it obvious to the examiner that nothing is missing.
